title: Regional proxy fabric and data-path segmentation reference
author: Maya Chen
summary: A reference architecture and operational guide for deploying a regional proxy fabric that segments tenant data paths, enforces egress controls, and provides graceful fallback to Redwood-hosted inference for private (VPC / on-prem) deployments.
content:
Overview

This page describes the Regional Proxy Fabric and Data-Path Segmentation reference architecture for Redwood Private deployments. It is intended for operators, platform engineers, and customer field teams who are implementing VPC or on-prem private installs that require strong tenant isolation, controlled egress, and resilient fallbacks to hosted services.

Goals

- Provide a network and service topology that isolates tenant data flows while minimizing blast radius for failures.
- Support controlled egress and 'data ejection' patterns for model refreshes, telemetry, and optional hosted fallbacks.
- Enable safe upgrades and quick rollback with minimal customer impact.
- Define measurable SLOs, observability signals, and day-2 operational runbooks.

Scope and applicability

This architecture applies to:
- Private VPC deployments (cloud-hosted customer VPC peering / transit scenarios).
- On-premise/private datacenter installs where a local control plane or sidecar control connectivity is used.
It does NOT attempt to replace tenant-level RBAC or customer-specific compliance rules; rather, it prescribes a network and service pattern that integrates with customer controls.

Terminology

- rwdn-proxy-fabric: Ensemble of proxy nodes (L7) that route inference requests to local runtime clusters or to hosted fallbacks.
- rwdn-edge-agent: Lightweight operator-managed agent on tenant subnets responsible for KV cache invalidation, telemetry batching, and health checks.
- data-ejection: The controlled transfer of specific telemetry or model artifacts to Redwood-hosted sinks under customer-approved contracts.
- surgical-fallback: Traffic-level switch to a hosted model variant when local resources are degraded.

High-level architecture (text diagram)

Customer VPC / On-prem Network --> [rwdn-edge-agent] --> [rwdn-proxy-fabric (regional)] --> {Local runtime cluster | Hosted fallback} --> Observability & KMS

Key components and responsibilities

1) rwdn-proxy-fabric (regional)
- Stateful L7 proxies (recommended: 3+ nodes per AZ/zone) that perform:
  - Tenant-aware routing (based on tenant-id header / mTLS SAN).
  - Per-tenant rate limiting and fairness policies.
  - Local prefix/KV cache routing decisions (TTL: configurable).
  - Egress gating: policy engine decides whether to allow data-ejection or to block external sinks.
- Failure modes: when a proxy loses connectivity to runtime, it signals a degraded state and applies surgical-fallback rules.

2) rwdn-edge-agent
- Deploy as a DaemonSet (Kubernetes) or systemd-managed service (bare metal).
- Responsibilities: health heartbeat to regional control plane, local sampling for telemetry, ephemeral credential management for KMS-bound operations.
- Security: enforce kernel-level network policies (iptables/update) to prevent direct egress from tenant subnets unless approved.

3) Control Plane (regional/tenant-aware)
- Policy service holds per-tenant routing rules, fallback thresholds, and egress allow-lists.
- KMS broker handles ephemeral session keys for model artifact access and data-ejection.

Security and compliance controls

- Mutual TLS (mTLS) for all inter-service traffic. Certificate issuance via customer PKI (recommended) or Redwood-managed short-lived certs per deployment.
- KMS integration: support for AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSM. Documented key rotation cadence: rotate master wrapping keys every 90 days, session keys every 24 hours.
- Egress allow-listing and ejection approval: any data-ejection flow requires an on-file approval form (see related_pages).

SLOs and thresholds (recommended defaults)

| Metric | Target | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Regional rwdn-proxy p95 latency | < 120 ms | measured at ingress-to-forwarding decision |
| Successful tenant requests (availability) | >= 99.95% | counted over 30d windows |
| Time-to-surgical-fallback | < 10 s | time from degraded signal to traffic steering |
| KV cache hit-rate (inference prefix) | >= 70% | workload dependent |

Operational patterns: surgical-fallback and ejection

Surgical-fallback intent: when local runtime cluster capacity or health drops below configurable thresholds, the proxy fabric will shift a tenant’s traffic to a hosted-compatible model variant that respects privacy constraints. Fallback must:
- Preserve tenant headers and do not forward any raw customer-provided PII to unapproved external sinks.
- Use model variants that have been vetted for token-level privacy equivalence (customer agreement required).

Data-ejection policy pattern:
- Allowed only if customer has signed ejection agreement.
- Ejection flows are routed through a dedicated egress node that applies DLP-style filters, scrubbers, and audit stamping.
- All ejection transfers logged and provenanced to support compliance audits.

Configuration / example snippets

1) Example proxy routing rule (YAML-style snippet)
proxyRules:
  - tenantId: "acme-corp"
    routePriority: 10
    runtimeCandidates: ["local-cluster-01","local-cluster-02"]
    fallback: {type: "hosted-compat", modelTag: "redwood-compat-v2", allowedEgress: false}
    rateLimit: {requestsPerSecond: 50}

2) Edge agent systemd unit (excerpt)
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Edge Agent
After=network-online.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rwdn-edge-agent --control-plane=cp.region.example.internal --agent-id=%H
Restart=on-failure

Testing, validation and acceptance criteria

Pre-installation checks (operator-run):
1) Network path verification: verify that the customer VPC routing maps tenant subnets to the edge agent subnets and that egress is gated by proxy IPs. Use: `curl -sS --resolve proxy.region.customer:443:10.0.1.5 https://proxy.region.customer/health`
2) KMS handshake: confirm that the control plane can decrypt a test-wrapped token.
3) Cert provisioning: ensure mTLS certs are present and that SAN / tenant mapping is correct.

Smoke validation (post-install):
1) Deploy synthetic workload (per-tenant): 10 TPS for 10 minutes, validate 2xx success >= 99% and p95 latency < 150ms.
2) Validate surgical-fallback: deliberately saturate local runtime to trigger fallback and measure time-to-fallback < target.
3) Ejection test (if enabled): attempt small telemetry ejection and confirm audit log entry and checksum match.

Upgrade and rollback guidance

Principles:
- Prefer blue/green or canary operator model for rwdn-proxy-fabric and rwdn-edge-agent.
- Always capture snapshots of policy state and KV-cache manifests before changes.
- Maintain a validated fallback path so rollback can be executed without requiring code reversion of hosted components.

Standard upgrade procedure (summary):
1) Create a policy snapshot: `rwdnctl policy snapshot --out policies-YYYYMMDD.json`
2) Deploy canary proxies to a single AZ (10% of traffic weight) and run synthetic workload for 20 minutes.
3) Monitor SLOs and error budgets; if errors exceed threshold (>= 1% elevated 5xx), abort and rollback.
4) If canary is healthy, ramp to 50% and then to 100% over 2h with health gates at each step.

Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Run `rwdnctl routes promote --from previous-proxies --to all-zones` to rebind traffic immediately.
2) If control plane state is inconsistent, restore policy snapshot: `rwdnctl policy restore --from policies-YYYYMMDD.json`.
3) Open an emergency incident (see escalation below) if KV-cache mismatches or tenant-level errors persist for > 15m.

Day-2 operations checklist

Daily
- Verify proxy health: all proxies with lastHeartbeat < 60s flagged.
- Check ejection audit log for any unapproved transfers.

Weekly
- Rotate ephemeral session keys (automated) and verify KMS rotation logs.
- Review policy drift: diff control-plane snapshot with live rules.

On-call runbook (short)

1) Symptom: elevated p99 latency for a tenant.
  - Step 1: check rwdn-proxy-fabric metrics for 5xx spikes and CPU/connection queue length.
  - Step 2: if proxies healthy, inspect local runtime node health; scale up runtime replicas or evict problematic models.
  - Step 3: if runtime is degraded and cannot recover in 5 minutes, trigger surgical-fallback for affected tenant: `rwdnctl fallback trigger --tenant acme-corp --mode hosted-compat`.

2) Symptom: accidental egress to disallowed host.
  - Step 1: disable egress node via control-plane console.
  - Step 2: capture packet-level evidence (pcap) and forward to security with audit id.
  - Step 3: notify customer and follow restricted-incident-response checklist.

Acceptance checklist for customer handoff (table)

| Item | Operator verification | Customer sign-off required? |
|---|---|---:|
| mTLS certs issued and verified | `openssl s_client -connect proxy:443` returns valid SAN | Yes |
| Egress allow-list configured | Control-plane policy shows egress entries | Yes |
| KMS integration tested | Roundtrip encrypt/decrypt test passed | Yes |
| Surgical-fallback validated | Measured fallback time < 10s | No (operator provides evidence) |

Appendix: quick-check automation scripts

1) Canary health check example (bash)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for i in {1..20}; do
  status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://proxy.region.customer/readiness)
  if [[ "$status" == "200" ]]; then
    echo "proxy ready"; exit 0
  fi
  sleep 6
done
echo "proxy not ready"; exit 1

2) Policy snapshot command examples
- `rwdnctl policy snapshot --out /tmp/policies-$(date +%F).json`
- `rwdnctl policy diff --since /tmp/policies-YYYYMMDD.json`
